text: Case operator supplied 19 docx files across three upload batches: 12 numbered/unnumbered Deep Research Snapshots (several exact duplicates), a Continuing Investigation Question Bank v1.0, a GIPA Primary Record Acquisition Pack v1.0, an AE Primary Record Acquisition Register RUN001, and two Answer Registers (A-K and L-T, RUN001, several duplicate uploads of A-K). Deduplicated by md5sum before reading anything - found 16 unique files behind the 24 uploaded copies.

Initial docx-to-text extraction via unzip + XML tag stripping lost every citation URL (the source registers only showed the literal word "Source" where a hyperlink had been). Re-extracted with a hyperlink-aware script that reads word/_rels/document.xml.rels and inlines each hyperlink's actual target URL - recovered real, checkable URLs for the numbered source lists in Snapshot 1 and Snapshot 2.

Read the full corpus. This is a mature, already-analysed investigation into whether Michael Kemp MP's "Bring Police Drones to the Mid North Coast" petition is evidentially supported: it audits the Moree PolAir-Remote trial's claimed 50% crime drop, 100+ arrests, 70+ stolen vehicles, six missing people, 30-60 second deployment, and helicopter-cost-fraction claims against the public record, and separately investigates privacy/AI/biometric governance, statewide procurement (EOI YR-2026-0058), political provenance, and oversight architecture. The corpus already ran its own DFAPTI-style evidence pass (F-001 to F-230 findings) and a DFAPTA-style analysis pass (referenced as "AR-063" in the Question Bank), then produced a 763-question bank and two Answer Registers resolving 519 of those questions.

Decided not to mechanically transcribe all 230 findings and 763 questions into individual register entries in this first pass - see DEC-0002. Instead promoted the 15 RESOLVED answer-register items, the strongest VERIFIED/FACT findings, and the two clearest messaging contradictions into a curated Evidence Register, Chronology, Contradiction Register and Open Question Register. The full corpus is preserved in full so later runs can promote more.

Resolved this repository's standing open architecture question (README.md, since the repository's earliest structure): a second case gets its own cases/<CASE-ID>/data/ directory rather than sharing the repository-root data/ or living in a separate repository. Added scripts/case-registry.js and reworked scripts/validate.js and scripts/generate-relationship-map.js to run per-case. See DEC-0019 in DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001's own decision register and DEC-0003 here.

Per the live/frozen-snapshot gating model, only the DFAPTI (evidence) workspace is built for this case now. DFAPTA, Lattice Atlas, the Temporal Projection Integrity Engine, Enforcement Notice, and Advocacy Package are not built until the operator issues an explicit freeze command for this case. See DEC-0004.

Every evidence item added in this run carries verification_state "Unverified" - see DEC-0001. Nothing here has been independently re-fetched or re-searched by this investigation; it is recorded as a faithful, honestly-labelled ingestion of a separate AI system's research, not as this investigation's own confirmed findings. GIPA Application 1-6 (EV-0034) is this case's concrete plan for converting the highest-value unresolved items into primary records.

Snapshot 7 (MAYHEM-MNC-POLAIR-REMOTE-DEEP-RESEARCH-SNAPSHOT-7-2026-08-16.docx, covering findings F-091 through F-140) was referenced by Snapshot 8 as its exact predecessor but was never supplied to this repository. This is a known gap in the preserved corpus - if the operator has that file, supplying it would let a future run fill in the missing findings range.

Case operator supplied MAYHEM-MNC-POLAIR-REMOTE-DEEP-RESEARCH-SNAPSHOT-7-2026-08-16.docx, closing the NOTE-0008 gap. Hash-checked against every already-preserved file first - confirmed genuinely new, not a re-upload of something already ingested.

Snapshot 7 (findings F-131-F-140) is the policy-feedback/technology-ratchet branch: PolAir-Remote continued operating well past its own stated six-month window (a 2 August 2026 incident, reported 5 August); a second procurement instrument (EOI YR-2026-0012, Aviation Command Operating Model Review) predates the RPAS Panel EOI by five weeks; the RPAS Panel EOI itself was published before the Moree consultation had closed; NSW Police leadership contemplated statewide scaling from the trial's first day; and no public stop/failure/decommissioning criteria were found anywhere in the material checked.

Snapshot 7 itself explicitly states the 'assess first' (Police Minister, early June) and 'prepare to scale' (EOI published 2 June) sequence is not contradictory, since the EOI is market research rather than a purchase decision - declined to register it as a Contradiction Register entry despite the surface tension, per the source's own explicit qualification. Recorded as interpretive context on EV-0039 instead. See DEC-0005.

Operator feedback: 'Evidence Register is almost empty compared with all the evidence given.' Correct - RUN-0001/DEC-0002's curation call under-delivered. Starting a full-corpus expansion pass rather than defending the original compact register.

Built a parser to extract every numbered finding (F-001-F-230) from the preserved snapshot text, handling three distinct formats used across the twelve snapshots: compact one-line 'F-XXX - CLASSIFICATION: statement' (Snapshot 3's cumulative F-001-F-043 register), 'F-XXX - title / body paragraph' with no per-item citation (Snapshots 4, 5, 7-12), and 'FINDING NN - title / Classification: / body / Source: <url>' with real per-finding URLs (Snapshot 6 only).

Snapshot 6 (F-091-F-130, economic/incapacitation/deterrence/political-feedback branch) was completely unmined in RUN-0001 and turned out to have the corpus's best evidentiary quality - every finding cites real, checkable NSW Audit Office, BOCSAR, Buy NSW and NSW Parliament URLs. Produced 29 new Source Register entries (SRC-0044-SRC-0072).

Ingested all 230 findings (EV-0043-EV-0262). Playwright-tested the live workspace at this scale: loads in ~2s, all 262 cards render, filtering works correctly. The 519-item Answer Register (RESOLVED/PARTIAL/OPEN across all 763 Question Bank items) remains the next under-mined layer if further depth is wanted - see DEC-0006.

Operator: 'yes, ingest the answer registers too'. Extending RUN-0003's full-coverage approach to the two Answer Register documents (519 classified Question Bank items) rather than selectively promoting only RESOLVED/PARTIAL items.

Parsed both Answer Register files (A-K: Q1-Q312, L-T: Q313-Q519). Status counts matched the corpus's own reported RUN 001 totals exactly: 15 RESOLVED, 70 PARTIAL, 373 OPEN - PRIMARY RECORD, 61 OPEN - ANALYTICAL. Confirms the parser captured all 519 items correctly with no loss or duplication.

Evidence Register now 781 items (EV-0001-EV-0781). Playwright-tested: loads in ~2.9s, all cards render, filtering ~400ms - still fully usable at this scale. The external research corpus supplied for this case is now essentially completely represented in the live register.

Operator: 'atomize'. Breaking the AE Register (40 per-question acquisition-status entries) and GIPA Pack (6 applications) out of their current single-summary evidence items (EV-0034/EV-0035) into individually addressable entries, completing full-corpus ingestion.

Every document in the originally supplied corpus is now atomized into the live Evidence Register: 230 snapshot findings, 519 answer-register items, 40 AE register entries, and 6 GIPA applications - 827 evidence items total, all still verification_state "Unverified" pending independent confirmation (DEC-0001).

Operator: 'freeze evidence register and proceed with gates'. Freezing at EV-0001-EV-0827 as Cycle 1's boundary (DEC-0009) and beginning Stages 2-6: DFAPTA, Lattice Atlas, Temporal Projection Integrity Engine, Enforcement Notice, Advocacy Package - cloning each stage's exact mechanism from DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001 rather than inventing new page styles, per this repository's established rule.

Operator: "the advocacy package has complaints instead of remedies and the others are empty", then "nothing about MAYHEM is a complaint machine". Rewrote Enforcement Notice (Recipients, Part Three, Part Four, nav label) and Advocacy Package (Who Has Standing, How to Submit) to state binding remedy demands and preconditions per recipient instead of information/confirmation requests. See DEC-0010.

Operator uploaded 6 new docx files. Identified 2 as genuinely new (DFAPTI Snapshot 001: 18 pinpoint-sourced evidence entries; Pre-Rollout Decision Architecture: a 13-gate external decision-sufficiency framework) and 4 as duplicate-content files sharing one filename, all covering the already-frozen Q313-Q519 range with no new citations - caused by the external ChatGPT session losing continuity rather than producing the actual missing Answer Register U-to-AF (Q520-Q763). Cross-checked all 18 Snapshot 001 items against the existing register before acting: 8 upgraded existing entries with pinpoint URLs, 7 added as new evidence (EV-0828-EV-0834), 3 needed no action (already captured with matching citations). See DEC-0011, RUN-0008, CHG-0007.

Operator: 'then instead continue DFAPTI' (declining to chase the missing Answer Register U-to-AF from the continuity-broken ChatGPT session). Ran this case's first live, this-session WebSearch pass across the highest-value open questions. Two genuine finds: the petition's headline statistics (50%/100+ arrests/70+ vehicles/six missing) trace to Kemp's own party's press release, not any NSW Police publication (EV-0835); and independent ASPI commentary raises DJI vendor/data-sovereignty governance questions about the trial (EV-0836). Everything else searched (formal evaluation, operational policy, PIA/facial recognition, EOI YR-2026-0058 award, LECC/Ombudsman/Audit Office examination, Aviation Command Operating Model Review findings, e-petition tabling status) came back negative or inconclusive, reinforcing rather than closing the case's existing open questions. WebFetch is confirmed broadly blocked in this sandbox (tested against 5 target URLs plus a control fetch of example.com), so these findings are WebSearch-summarised paraphrase, not verbatim primary-source quotation - recorded honestly as such (DEC-0012).

Operator requested a quality-control review of the Enforcement Notice's rigor - whether claims stay within what the evidence register supports, whether fact is distinguished from judgement, and whether the framing is systemic rather than allegatory. Reviewed the full document section by section. It held up: locatability-only claims in Part One, statutory grounding for every remedy in Part Three, procedural (not punitive) demands in Part Four, and an explicit sender checklist in Part Six. One gap: the verification_state "Unverified" disclosure (DEC-0001) existed only in the closing Evidentiary Basis section, where a reader of the substantive Parts One-Four - including the notice's actual recipients - could miss it. See DEC-0013 for the finding and the fix (a verification-status notice moved to immediately after the opening summary).

Operator raised a fix-not-fight framing concern about naming Michael Kemp MP on the public structural-patterns page: describing the "Kemp's bail laws" label as "politically convenient" ascribes strategic motive, which risks personal backlash and is inconsistent with this case's own no-intent-claimed standard. Reworded to "widely used" in both AR-008 (analysis.json) and the SHM Gate Definitional Control match_note - the finding that the label misdescribes the actual statute (s 22C) is unchanged, only the motive-implying adjective was removed. Also added Michael Kemp MP's name to the public structural-patterns page's Definitional Control card, in his public/official capacity as the petition's own campaign author, per the same neutral standard. See DEC-0014.

Starting scheduled automated pass. Ran resume.js for both registered cases; chose DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001 (18/18 open questions still Open, last live run RUN-0009 on 2026-08-17) over DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001 (worked yesterday, RUN-0067). Plan: sweep WebSearch across the case's highest-value still-open questions and threads per DEC-0014, attempt WebFetch on any promising URL to check whether this session's egress block (DEC-0008/DEC-0012) still holds.

WebFetch returned EGRESS_BLOCKED on parliament.nsw.gov.au, haveyoursay.nsw.gov.au, moreeonlinenews.com.au, and a control fetch of example.com - confirming the block is a blanket session-level constraint, not site-specific bot detection, consistent with DEC-0008/DEC-0012/RUN-0009. No further fetch attempts made against these domains this run; continuing with WebSearch-derived findings only, flagged as such on every new evidence item, per DEC-0006's rule against working around access blocks.

Located a 16 July 2026 sponsored-content article by Brendan Moylan MP (Member for Northern Tablelands, NSW Nationals shadow minister for agriculture and prevention of regional crime), syndicated across the Australian Community Media regional network. This is the same 'Brendan Moylan' already quoted at EV-0011/CTR-0002 - his political role and the paid-placement nature of that source were not previously identified in the register. The article's fuller quote names SAR and MVA response alongside crime-fighting, and separately credits the trial with a ~19-20% two-year crime-reduction figure distinct from the already-registered 50% (petition) and 53%-since-2022 (EV-0053) figures. Registered as EV-0837/EV-0838/CHR-0021.

Located the exact YR-2026-0012 procurement URL plus two dates not previously registered (close 4 May 2026; estimated decision 1 July 2026, now over seven weeks past with no located public output). Registered as EV-0839, supplementing EV-0038/EV-0196.

A first WebSearch summary attributed a '$100,000' Moree trial total-cost figure to the Moylan article; a second, independent WebSearch query on the same article returned no mention of any dollar figure. Since the two summaries disagree and neither can be checked against verbatim text (WebFetch blocked), the figure was not registered - consistent with DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001's DEC-0007 standing rule against merging an unconfirmed or self-contradicting search-summary claim. Q-0004 remains Open, unchanged from EV-0231 (official cost not finalised as at 30 July 2026 per NSW Parliament).

A biometrics trade publication (Biometric Update) raises general drone/facial-recognition integration risk without alleging actual PolAir-Remote integration. A separate NSW development (national driver-licence face-matching network expansion, NDLFRS) surfaced in the same search sweep; checked and confirmed it is a distinct system from PolAir-Remote drone imagery with no located connection between the two, and excluded from being merged into the same evidence item to avoid an AI-summary conflation error. Registered as EV-0840, Q-0006 remains Open.

Q-0001 (Moree trial evaluation), Q-0013 (EOI YR-2026-0058 outcome) and Q-0009 (NSW Parliament e-petition tabling status) were each re-searched this run with fresh query wording and returned no new result beyond what RUN-0009 already established - search-exhausted for this pass, not re-logged as separate evidence. Run complete; proceeding to validate.js and commit.

Scheduled automated pass. Chose DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001 over DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001 this run to keep collection cadence roughly even: BB was worked most recently (RUN-0068, 2026-08-22), while MNC's last live-collection run was RUN-0010 (2026-08-21) and still carries all 18 open questions Open. Confirmed via a live control fetch (example.com) that WebFetch remains EGRESS_BLOCKED this session, same as every prior run since DEC-0008/DEC-0012; no attempt made to route around it per DEC-0006. All evidence this run is recorded from WebSearch's own summarised results with hash_exception_reason flagged, same discipline as prior runs.

Ran a 16-query WebSearch sweep (SRCH-0022 to SRCH-0037) per DEC-0014's full-surface cadence, covering Q-0004, Q-0005, Q-0007, Q-0009, Q-0010, Q-0011, Q-0012, Q-0013, Q-0014, Q-0015, Q-0017, Q-0018, Q-0002/Q-0003, and THR-03/04/05/06/07/08/09/10/11/12 - deliberately targeting angles (Q-0007, Q-0010, Q-0011, Q-0015, Q-0017) not yet swept in SRCH-0001-0021 (RUN-0009/RUN-0010), alongside re-checks of previously-tried angles with fresh query wording.

Located a named, on-the-record source for EV-0224's previously uncited claim that the Police Minister identified Kempsey as a possible future expansion location: Minister for Police Yasmin Catley, quoted in the Macleay Argus saying she would be guided by police on any expansion and felt confident Kempsey would 'certainly be looked at very strongly'. Registered as EV-0841, cross-linked to EV-0224.

Located reporting that NSW Police has used conventional (non-PolAir-Remote) drones in Kempsey and regionally since 2016 via a dedicated RPAS Support Unit, including a specific traffic-enforcement drone operation at Cochrane Street/Kemp Street, Kempsey (31 infringements in ~75 minutes). Registered as EV-0842 - sharpens Q-0007 by distinguishing existing conventional drone use in Kempsey from the fixed-dock PolAir-Remote model the petition seeks.

Identified the content of SRC-0017 (NSW Parliament Q&A tracking id=108055), previously registered as a source but not yet captured as evidence: the government's answer reportedly directs the questioner to the NSW Police Force Annual Report for financial information rather than stating a cost figure - a second, independently-numbered parliamentary record pointing the same way as EV-0012 (id=108763). Registered as EV-0843.

Located a second, distinct ASPI Strategist piece from EV-0836, specifically on DJI/Chinese-drone data sovereignty ('Australia is flying blind on Chinese drone data', coverage dated 25 July 2026 by DroneXL): ASPI argues Australia has no visibility into where Chinese-made-drone data ends up and calls for a partial ban on Chinese drone companies. No NSW Police response to this specific framing located. Registered as EV-0844.

Located a jec.org.au page distinct from EV-0033's own formal submission: a republish/commentary on 'The Land' reporting that frames drone trials as set to expand, quoting Justice and Equity Centre Principal Solicitor Jonathan Hall Spence that serious privacy risks need to be accounted for before any further expansion. Registered as EV-0845, relevant to Q-0007/Q-0012/Q-0015.

Located a third, distinct youth-crime statistic beyond the petition's 50% figure (EV-0835) and Moylan's ~19-20%-over-two-years figure (EV-0838): a Macleay Argus report of a 33% 12-month rise in Kempsey youth crime and court legal actions against young people rising from 154 (12mo to June 2024) to 205 (12mo to June 2025). Registered as EV-0846 - the continued proliferation of differently-scoped percentage claims across independent sources deepens rather than resolves Q-0002/Q-0003's statistic-provenance question.

Negative/no-change findings this pass, not separately logged as evidence: Q-0001 (no formal Moree trial evaluation report located, same as RUN-0009/RUN-0010), Q-0013/EOI YR-2026-0058 outcome (no supplier-award record located), Q-0014 (no LECC/Ombudsman/Audit Office complaint review of PolAir-Remote located), Q-0005 (no formal SOP/policy document text located, only the general central-Aviation-Command/local-request architecture already at EV-0135), Q-0017 (no publicly stated stop/decommissioning criteria or six-month extension notice located beyond what RUN-0009 already found), Q-0009 (no NSW Parliament e-petition tabling record located for the Kemp petition specifically, same as RUN-0009/RUN-0010), and Q-0018/EOI YR-2026-0012 (re-confirmed the same close date 4 May 2026/estimated decision 1 July 2026 already registered at EV-0839, no outcome record located - the missed self-stated deadline stands unchanged). These questions are search-exhausted for this pass, not newly closed. Run complete; proceeding to validate.js and commit.

Added Yield Catalogue framing to this case's Enforcement Notice (before any recipient or remedy demand) and Advocacy Package (naming its own components - Evidence Register, Five-Step Verification, non-allegatory framing - as Citizen Tools already delivered, independent of enforcement outcome). Applied identically across every case with a built Enforcement Notice, per the operator's instruction to apply the Yield Catalogue everywhere rather than to a single case. See DEC-0015.

Built this case's Yield Gate: a genuine assessment of all 11 Discovered Functions and 19 Citizen Tools against this case's own DFAPTA, Lattice Atlas and SHM Gate content. Noted where this case's prospective, policy-audit character produces a differently-shaped match than a retrospective harm case would - e.g. Structural Literacy as a Preventative Tool matches more strongly here than anywhere else in this repository, since this case audits a proposal before it is finalised rather than documenting a completed harm. See DEC-0016.

Following the protocol correction applied to DFAPTI-BB-FF-2026-00001 today, checked this case's own DFAPTA against the same standard before the operator asked: 22 paths anchor only 102 of 827 frozen evidence items (12.3% coverage). Reported this to the operator, who confirmed ("Agreed about MNC") the same treatment should apply: remove downstream gates, rebuild DFAPTA toward genuine coverage. Removed SHM Gate, Yield Gate, Lattice Atlas, Temporal Projection Integrity Engine, Enforcement Notice and Advocacy Package (DEC-0017). Unlike BB-FF's original nine paths, these 22 are specific and accurate, not generic - retained as Pass 1 rather than discarded. Also fixed every site-wide reference to the removed pages: catalogue/index.html and yield-catalogue/index.html's 'Where this is applied' lists, and withdrew public-interest/structural-patterns/index.html's Mid North Coast section (built directly on the now-removed SHM Gate) pending rebuild.

Resumed both registered cases (resume.js) to choose today's DFAPTI pass. DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001's last genuine evidence-collection run was RUN-0071 (2026-08-24, yesterday); DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001's last genuine collection run was RUN-0011 (2026-08-23) - its intervening RUN-0012/0013/0014 were non-evidentiary site-framing/Yield-Gate/DFAPTA-Pass-2 work, not collection passes. Per this repository's own established cadence-balancing practice (see RUN-0071's and RUN-0011's own notes), and because MNC still carries all 18 open questions Open against BB's 8 of 9, chose DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001 for this run. Per this run's own operating instructions, only DFAPTI (evidence-register-level) work is in scope for this case - Stages 2-6 (dfapta/, etc.) are untouched regardless of their current build state.

Confirmed via a live control fetch (example.com) that WebFetch remains EGRESS_BLOCKED in this session, consistent with every prior run since DEC-0006/DEC-0008/DEC-0012; WebSearch functions normally. No attempt made to route around the block, per DEC-0006. Ran a 21-query multi-angle sweep (SRCH-0038 to SRCH-0058) per DEC-0014's full-surface cadence, covering Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, Q-0004, Q-0005, Q-0006, Q-0008, Q-0009, Q-0010, Q-0012, Q-0013, Q-0014, Q-0018 and THR-01/02/03/04/05/06/07/09/10/12, deliberately using fresh wording rather than repeating RUN-0011's queries.

Located a previously-unregistered NSW Parliament document - 'Answers to Supplementary QONs - Budget Estimates - Minister for Police' (received 26 March 2026), registered as SRC-0096 - whose WebSearch-indexed content appears to address exactly the gaps THR-05/THR-06 have been probing: PolAir-Remote's public/private-space operating distinction and 'no proactive policing of private spaces' position (EV-0847, relevant to CTR-0001/Q-0005/Q-0010), and a named 'AI and Emerging Biometrics Ethics Board' reviewing Artificial Intelligence Assessment Framework determinations (EV-0848, relevant to Q-0006/Q-0012). WebFetch to parliament.nsw.gov.au returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, so only WebSearch's own paraphrase of the document could be reviewed, not verbatim text - both evidence items are recorded 'Requires Verification'/'Unverified' and quote only the paraphrase, explicitly labelled as such, rather than inventing a verbatim excerpt. Neither question is closed: this narrows what the controlling policy document and any PolAir-Remote-specific AIAF determination should say, it does not supply either document itself.

Also investigated and declined to register a distinct claim: multiple WebSearch result summaries this run stated the Moree trial's six-month cost as '$100,000', but no specific linked article's title or snippet actually surfaces that figure with attribution, and it directly conflicts with EV-0012/EV-0843's own already-registered finding that a 30 July 2026 NSW Parliament answer stated the total trial cost had 'not yet been finalised'. Treated as an unverifiable/likely search-summary artefact rather than evidence, per this investigation's standing discipline against merging an AI tool's own unattributed synthesis into the register (see DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001 RUN-0065's AI-summary-conflation discipline) - Q-0004 remains Open and unresolved by this run.

Negative/search-exhausted findings this pass, not separately logged as evidence: Q-0001 (still no located formal Moree trial evaluation report), Q-0008 (full 11 August 2026 Macleay Argus article still not accessible - paywalled, and WebFetch blocked), Q-0009 (no NSW Parliament e-petition tabling record found for the Kemp petition), Q-0013 (EOI YR-2026-0058 outcome still undisclosed as at this run), Q-0014 (no LECC/Ombudsman/IPC/Audit Office PolAir-Remote-specific finding located), Q-0018 (EOI YR-2026-0012/Aviation Command Operating Model Review outcome still undisclosed), and no Kempsey/Bellbrook Aboriginal Land Council-specific consultation record located for Q-0015/THR-08 beyond confirming the Land Council itself exists. The already-registered ~53% Moree youth-legal-actions decline (EV-0018/EV-0838) was reproduced again under fresh wording with no new drone-specific causal attribution found (Q-0002/THR-03).

Automated DFAPTA Pass 2 sub-pass (DEC-0019). Read dfapta/analysis.json's status field first ("In Progress - Pass 2", not Frozen - proceeded), then all 18 prior decisions.json entries, all 50 prior investigation_notes.json entries, all 15 automation_log.json entries, and source_register.json in full, before treating anything as new, per DEC-0009/DEC-0010's standing correction. Automated DFAPTA Pass 2 sub-pass (DEC-0020). Read dfapta/analysis.json's status field first ("In Progress - Pass 2", not Frozen - proceeded), then all 19 prior decisions.json entries, all 51 prior investigation_notes.json entries, all 16 automation_log.json entries, and source_register.json in full, before treating anything as new, per DEC-0009/DEC-0010's standing correction. The evidence register was unchanged at 848 items since the prior sub-pass. Rather than re-treading the snapshot files Pass 2's first sub-pass already worked, computed anchor coverage per primary-source file and found preserved/answer-register-a-to-k-run001.txt - the case's own Continuing Investigation Question Bank Answer Register, 312 evidence items across eleven sections - only 5/312 anchored despite being the largest single unexploited primary-source file in the case. Read the full file section by section (all eleven sections, Q1-Q312) before deciding scope, per the protocol's requirement to work from the actual primary-source text rather than a topic label.

Scope decision for this sub-pass: Section A ("Moree Trial Evaluation", Q1-Q47) was entirely unanchored and is independently identified by the register's own "RUN 001 CONTROL FINDING" as the single highest-priority acquisition gap in the case - ahead of PolAir-specific policy/SOPs, mission-level flight/outcome data, and the PIA/AI/cyber/vendor assessments covered by the file's remaining ten sections (Sections B-K, roughly 260 further evidence items, and the separate answer-register-l-to-t-run001.txt file, remain open for subsequent sub-passes). Chose to close Section A completely (all 47 questions, six paths grouped by natural sub-topic: evaluator existence/independence, pre-deployment criteria, analytic design, and two clusters of undisclosed outcome measures, plus the publication/decision-control gap) rather than sample a few questions from several sections, on the view that a fully closed, coherent section is more genuinely useful and less generic than partial coverage spread thin - consistent with the operator's standing correction that a path count without real depth is exactly the failure this routine exists to avoid. Cross-referenced each new path against existing paths before writing to avoid duplicating ground already covered: AR-006 (causal attribution gap), AR-014 (continuation beyond the six-month window), AR-020 (child/Indigenous data governance), AR-023 and AR-024 (untested alternative causal mechanisms) each connect to specific new findings in this pass without restating them.

Automated DFAPTA Pass 2 sub-pass (DEC-0021). Read dfapta/analysis.json's status field first ("In Progress - Pass 2", not Frozen - proceeded), then all 20 prior decisions.json entries, all 53 prior investigation_notes.json entries, all 17 automation_log.json entries, and source_register.json in full, before treating anything as new, per DEC-0009/DEC-0010's standing correction. Evidence register unchanged at 848 items since the prior sub-pass. Continued from the prior sub-pass's own stated scope and read preserved/answer-register-a-to-k-run001.txt Section B, "Petition Claim Verification" (Q48-Q92, EV-0310-EV-0354), in full - the next unclosed section after Section A, and the least-anchored (only 3 of 45 items previously cited, all by AR-007). Read the full section text directly before deciding scope, per the protocol's requirement to work from primary-source material rather than a topic label.

Scope decision for this sub-pass: unlike Section A, most of Section B substantively duplicates Pass 1 analysis already on record rather than opening new ground. Q48-Q55 (the petition's "50%" figure lacking a disclosed measure, geography, offence set, age group or baseline/comparison dates) restates AR-003.3 almost item-for-item; Q56-Q59 (the decline predates the trial and neither NSW Police nor BOCSAR make the causal claim) restates AR-003.2 and AR-003's own analysis text; Q76-Q81 (the undefined 30-60-second deployment clock) restates AR-007, which already anchors three of that cluster's six items. Adding new paths to re-cite this ground would be exactly the padding-for-a-number failure this routine exists to avoid, so none was added - those 15 items (EV-0310-EV-0321, EV-0339-EV-0341) remain honestly unanchored rather than forced into a duplicate path. The section's remaining two clusters were read closely enough to confirm they add something AR-004 and AR-005 do not already state: Q68 and Q75 name a drone-contribution category (information already known to ground officers; a missing person located primarily by another resource after only initial assistance) that AR-004's three existing candidate meanings of "assisted" do not cover, and which - if it applies to any share of the aggregate - means the true drone-caused count could be smaller than any of AR-004's readings; Q85-Q92 name eight specific cost components (personnel, communications, the Remote Operations Centre, maintenance, data infrastructure, regulatory compliance, ground response, downstream justice-system costs) none of which is disclosed as included or excluded in the petition's cost comparison, more granular than AR-005's existing net-cost-per-prevented-harm framing.
